review.body:
### ARL13B re-review of `93cbb42` — one item remains

Two of the three blocking items are fixed, and the hardest one was fixed by doing the work rather than re-labelling the deferral.

**✅ The 7 `GO:0005829` cytosol rows are properly resolved.** The deferral was retired by walking the participant graph: `R-HSA-9640110` (misfolded ARL13B, Q3SXY8, cytosol) → `9640104` → set `9641091` → complex `9641099`, and `R-HSA-9641129` → subset `9641108` → set `9641120`. It also caught a distinction my earlier framing glossed over — `R-HSA-9646679`'s event compartment is the MTOC while the nested HDAC6/cargo components keep cytosol labels, and the row is justified on the component label. I still lean `MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED`, but now that Reactome is shown asserting cytosol on the ARL13B entity explicitly rather than propagating it onto an unexamined member set, `KEEP_AS_NON_CORE` is a defensible judgment call, not a policy breach. Not blocking.

**✅ Core function 1 fixed** — the non-hydrolyzable GTPγS exocyst co-IP line is gone and the description dropped the "engage effectors" conjunct. **✅ Spacing artifacts fixed** — zero remaining across YAML, notes and both history records. **✅ Notes de-processed** — the retrieval-provenance paragraph moved to the history record.

**🟡 IMPORTANT — the two PIFO `GO:0005515` rows (:61-108) still use `KEEP_AS_NON_CORE`.** `.claude/skills/annotation-reviewer/SKILL.md:186-199` allows only `MODIFY` (with an evidence-backed more-informative MF), otherwise `REMOVE` as uninformative, or `UNDECIDED` for unadjudicatable evidence. The rebuttal recorded in the history record — "genericity alone does not establish likely biological error" — is the exact reading the policy forecloses: "removal does not mean the reported interaction is false." The `UNDECIDED` carve-out cannot apply because you adjudicated the full text and confirmed the coassociation, and `MODIFY` is unavailable because the multi-partner pull-down (PIFO, Rab6, Rab8, γ-/β-tubulin, Centrin, Kif3a) supports no specific ARL13B activity. `REMOVE` with the supporting_text kept is the path, and it is fully compatible with the interaction being real. If you'd rather change the policy, that belongs in an issue against the skill rather than a silent per-gene exception.

**Withdrawing my 128-row objection.** I called the `UNDECIDED` on the interactome rows a blocker that doesn't bear on the decision. That was wrong on the policy text — I read past its last clause, "If the relevant evidence cannot be accessed or adjudicated, the standing `UNDECIDED` rule still applies." The pair records live in supplementary tables absent from the repo, which is exactly that case, so the asymmetry with PIFO is the policy working as written. No change needed there.

**🔵 Non-blocking:** `normal` still reads as pipeline vocabulary at `ARL13B-notes.md:27,29,41`; and `PMID_28487361.md:228` still argues GEF activity rather than hydrolysis is the Joubert-relevant core, which would reorder cores 1 and 2.

Fix the two PIFO rows and this is a strong review.

### ATP2B2 review — `aigr-pr-review` (re-review of `099a96c`)

**Approving.** Item 3a — the only blocker after the second round — is fixed exactly as scoped, and nothing regressed. Final tally across the same 58 source assertions and eight alternative products: **28 ACCEPT / 9 KEEP_AS_NON_CORE / 19 UNDECIDED / 1 MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED / 1 MODIFY** (58 ✓; one row moved `UNDECIDED`→`MODIFY`, nothing lost or invented).

✅ **`GO:0005515` / PMID:17689535 → `MODIFY` → `GO:0019903 protein phosphatase binding`** (yaml:161-190). The reason states both why the generic term is off and why the replacement fits. Verified: the quote reproduces `PMID_17689535.md:42-43` verbatim including the wrapped line and its trailing space; the P01258/CALCA discrepancy note and the `suggested_questions` entry are preserved unchanged, with no PPP3 accession guessed in; `MODIFY` is in `protein_binding_policy.py:41` `COMPLIANT_ACTIONS` and the `modified_terms` cross-check (`validator.py:885-901`) has nothing to trip on. The SCRIB row correctly stays `UNDECIDED`. Scope held: contextual regulatory binding, not a second core, and no NFAT-signalling process term added.

🔵 **One new suggestion.** The notes record that `GO:0030346 protein phosphatase 2B binding` was found in the hierarchy but its official definition could not be retrieved in the bounded check — I can resolve that: the term is real and used for exactly this relationship (`PPP3CB-goa.tsv`, `P16298` enables ECO:0000314; `SOD1-goa.tsv`, `P00441` IDA+IC). Calcineurin *is* PP2B, so the child is directly supported and the parent is one level broader than the evidence warrants. Not a correctness objection. 🔵 Carried: PMC2442823 is open access, so the PMCA2-specific ciliary claim behind the `GO:0005929` ACCEPT could be quoted rather than attested; deep research still not run (honestly disclosed, three primary sources added instead).

Across three rounds every substantive item was answered with evidence or with a recorded argument, never silently — the cilium item was closed by fetching a new primary source rather than adopting the framing I proposed, and the exosome counter-argument was better than my objection. This last commit is a good example of the distinction worth keeping: it changes the annotation while leaving the disputed supporting entity untouched and explicitly refusing to infer a replacement accession. No scope creep under review pressure.

Note: `just`/`uv` are not on PATH in this runner, so I could not re-run `just validate human ATP2B2`; `Build and test` is in progress on this head. The policy and cross-reference rules above were checked by hand against the validation source. Record remains `DRAFT` and no repo-wide validation pass is claimed, both as stated in the PR body.

Full detail: https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/pull/3554#issuecomment-5898853177

Item 3 (bulk evidence-linkage regression) — substantially addressed and closing. supporting_text 10 -> 20, reference findings 0 -> 8, and all 20 snippets verify verbatim against their caches. I accept the rationale in ATP6V0A2-notes.md:62 for not restoring the other 52 mechanically: evidence has to support the revised claim, and several old quotes backed claims this review no longer makes (the base GO:0005515 row's two quotes supported a REMOVE). Of the 11 PMID-backed rows, six carry a direct anchor and the rest are covered by reference-level findings; the remaining 20 are GO_REF/Reactome IEA rows with no PMID snippet to attach. The new findings are well scoped — PMID:39680136's separates the human HeLa localization from the mouse MEF pH measurement, and PMID:28296633's bounds the CRISPR/HIF row to aerobic culture.

Still open:

🟡 1. GO:0005515 is still KEEP_AS_NON_CORE (ATP6V0A2-ai-review.yaml:197-217), unchanged across all three commits on this branch. protein_binding_policy.py:43 sets COMPLIANT_ACTIONS = {MODIFY, REMOVE, UNDECIDED, PENDING} and names this action's failure mode verbatim at :51-54. The verified supported_by quote carries over either way.

I have raised this twice with a concrete fix and the notes reaffirm the choice deliberately. current_head_formal_reviews.body:
### Summary checklist

- [ ] Schema validation passes — **could not run locally** (`just`/`uv` not installed on this runner); relying on PR CI
- [x] All PMIDs verified as real — all 4 new caches resolve, titles/DOIs consistent
- [x] Supporting text matches publication content — all 7 `supporting_text` values verified verbatim
- [x] GO terms correct and specific — one questionable `MODIFY` (🟡 #3)
- [ ] Review actions well-justified — reasons are prose-only; annotation-level evidence anchors removed (🟡 #1)
- [x] Core functions accurately identified — the two core MFs are right; core function 2 is under-located (🔵 #5)
- [x] No over-annotation issues missed

Action tally checks out against GOA: 23 rows → 12 ACCEPT / 6 KEEP_AS_NON_CORE / 4 MODIFY / 1 UNDECIDED, all 23 present. Every `supporting_text` I checked is verbatim (`PMID:16640564` ×2, `PMID:7892223` ×2, `PMID:11738050`, `PMID:24598254`, `PMID:29056341`). The GO-CAM claim in the notes is correct — `gocams/index.tsv:9005` does put AUH in model `68b0f0d000007160` with `GO:0050011` + `GO:0110052`, so declining to add a pathway-completeness term is right.

### What improved

- `GO:0003824 catalytic activity` and `GO:0009083 branched-chain amino acid catabolic process` moved from `MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED` → `MODIFY` with concrete replacements. CLAUDE.md is explicit that an over-general term wants `MODIFY` + a replacement, so this is the correct reclassification.
- `GO:0004300 enoyl-CoA hydratase activity` → `KEEP_AS_NON_CORE`. The activity is genuinely measured in recombinant human AUH ("the recombinant protein showed a low degree of the enzymatic activity", `PMID:7892223`); low ≠ wrong, and non-core is the right slot.
- Retracting the "separate folded RNA-binding domain" claim is correct. `PMID:11738050` shows a lysine comb on helix H1 *within* the crotonase fold, not a distinct domain — the base review overstated `PMID:7892223`'s "distinct domains" phrasing.
- `GO:0006635` → `UNDECIDED` rather than asserting `PROPAGATION_BAD`/`FUNCTIONAL_DIVERGENCE` without inspecting the tree is the conservative reading CLAUDE.md's IBA section asks for.

### 🟡 IMPORTANT

**1. All annotation-level `supported_by` was deleted (25 → 2 occurrences; the 2 survivors are in `core_functions`).**

Every one of the 23 `existing_annotations[].review` blocks now carries a prose `reason` and **no evidence anchor**. Base `main` had verbatim quotes on ~10 of them. This matters beyond style: `supporting_text` is the one field the reference validator checks as a verbatim substring, so removing it moves the whole annotation block outside automated verification. Claims like:

- `genes/human/AUH/AUH-ai-review.yaml:42` — "The original human experiments establish weak enoyl-CoA hydratase activity"
- `genes/human/AUH/AUH-ai-review.yaml:56` — "consistent with direct human substrate assays"
- `genes/human/AUH/AUH-ai-review.yaml:265` — "shows its best measured activity on methylglutaconyl-CoA, with substrate kinetics reported in the normal abstract"

are all quotable from the caches (`PMID:7892223` "showed a low degree of the enzymatic activity"; `PMID:16640564` "The best substrates were (E)-3-MG-CoA (V(max) = 3.9 U.mg(-1)…"), and the base review did quote them. The skill's standard is that `ACCEPT`/`KEEP_AS_NON_CORE` need *positive support*, not just a narrative.

Relatedly, this probably breaks the PR's "one advisory" claim: `src/ai_gene_review/validation/validator.py:1103` warns on `ACCEPT` annotations whose `original_reference_id` is a PMID with no `supported_by` **when full text is available**. `GO:0005739` HTP / `PMID:34800366` (`AUH-ai-review.yaml:243-255`) is exactly that case — `publications/PMID_34800366.md` has `full_text_available: true`. Please re-run `just validate human AUH` and reconcile.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cmungall%2Fclingen-auh%2C%20in%20genes%2Fhuman%2FAUH%2FAUH-ai-review.yaml%2C%20restore%20supported_by%20evidence%20anchors%20to%20the%20existing_annotations%20review%20blocks.%20Every%20review%20whose%20reason%20asserts%20an%20experimental%20fact%20should%20carry%20a%20supported_by%20entry%20with%20a%20verbatim%20supporting_text%20substring%20from%20the%20cached%20publication%20in%20publications%2F.%20At%20minimum%20cover%3A%20the%20three%20GO%3A0004300%20rows%20%28PMID%3A7892223%29%2C%20the%20GO%3A0004490%20IDA%20and%20GO%3A0006552%20IMP%20rows%20%28PMID%3A16640564%29%2C%20the%20GO%3A0003730%20IDA%20row%20%28PMID%3A7892223%29%2C%20the%20GO%3A0005739%20HTP%20row%20%28PMID%3A34800366%2C%20which%20has%20full_text_available%20true%20and%20therefore%20trips%20the%20ACCEPT-without-supported_by%20validator%20warning%29%2C%20and%20the%20GO%3A0050011%20and%20GO%3A0110052%20TAS%20rows%20%28PMID%3A29056341%29.%20Then%20re-run%20just%20validate%20human%20AUH%20and%20report%20all%20warnings.&repo=ai4curation/ai-gene-review)

**2. Every `summary` was replaced by a restatement of the term plus the action.**

`summary: 'mitochondrion: accept.'`, `summary: 'RNA binding: modify.'`, `summary: 'mRNA 3''-UTR binding: accept.'` — 23 of 23. The schema calls this "Summary of the review" and marks it `recommended`, and the base version used it to say something ("Phylogenetic (IBA) assignment of mitochondrial localization. AUH is a well-established mitochondrial-matrix enzyme with an N-terminal transit peptide; this is correct though less specific than the matrix annotation."). The new form conveys nothing not already in `term.label` and `action`, and it is the field that surfaces in the rendered HTML. The `reason` fields are good — the summaries should state what the annotation asserts and whether it holds, not echo the action.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cmungall%2Fclingen-auh%2C%20in%20genes%2Fhuman%2FAUH%2FAUH-ai-review.yaml%2C%20rewrite%20all%2023%20existing_annotations%5B%5D.review.summary%20fields.%20They%20currently%20just%20restate%20the%20term%20label%20and%20the%20action%20%28e.g.%20%27mitochondrion%3A%20accept.%27%29%2C%20duplicating%20term.label%20and%20action.%20Replace%20each%20with%20a%20one-sentence%20statement%20of%20what%20the%20annotation%20asserts%2C%20what%20evidence%20route%20produced%20it%2C%20and%20whether%20it%20holds%20-%20keeping%20the%20existing%20reason%20fields%20unchanged.%20Then%20re-render%20with%20just%20render%20human%20AUH%20and%20re-validate.&repo=ai4curation/ai-gene-review)

**3. `MODIFY GO:0003723 RNA binding → GO:0003730 mRNA 3'-UTR binding` (`AUH-ai-review.yaml:72-87`) narrows away evidence the review itself relies on.**

- **Redundant.** `GO:0003730` is *already* an IDA annotation on AUH from `PMID:7892223` (`AUH-goa.tsv` row 21, reviewed at `AUH-ai-review.yaml:281-293` as `ACCEPT`). The `MODIFY` therefore proposes a term the gene already carries — it collapses the ARBA row into an existing annotation rather than adding information.
- **Internally inconsistent.** The review's own `description` says "AUH associates with mitochondrial RNA and ribosomes", and its `PMID:24598254` finding says "RNA and ribosome copurification … connect AUH to mitochondrial protein synthesis". `PMID:11738050` is titled "…a **single-stranded RNA binding** homolog of enoyl-CoA hydratase" and describes a lysine comb whose spacing matches RNA phosphate groups — backbone-generic ssRNA binding, not 3'-UTR-sequence-specific binding. `GO:0003723` is the only term in the annotation set covering the mitochondrial RNA / ssRNA binding this review argues for; refining it to `GO:0003730` deletes that coverage.

`ACCEPT` is the better action here — the parent is not uninformative redundancy in this case, because it covers binding events (mt-RNA, mitoribosome-associated RNA, generic ssRNA) that `GO:0003730` does not.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cmungall%2Fclingen-auh%2C%20in%20genes%2Fhuman%2FAUH%2FAUH-ai-review.yaml%20around%20lines%2072-87%2C%20change%20the%20GO%3A0003723%20RNA%20binding%20IEA%20annotation%20from%20MODIFY%20%28proposed%20replacement%20GO%3A0003730%29%20to%20ACCEPT.%20Rationale%20for%20the%20reason%20field%3A%20GO%3A0003730%20mRNA%203-UTR%20binding%20is%20already%20an%20independent%20IDA%20annotation%20on%20AUH%20from%20PMID%3A7892223%20so%20the%20MODIFY%20is%20redundant%3B%20and%20GO%3A0003723%20is%20the%20only%20term%20in%20the%20set%20covering%20the%20mitochondrial%20RNA%20and%20mitoribosome-associated%20RNA%20binding%20reported%20in%20PMID%3A24598254%20plus%20the%20single-stranded%20RNA%20binding%20lysine-comb%20mechanism%20in%20PMID%3A11738050.%20Add%20a%20supported_by%20entry%20with%20a%20verbatim%20quote%20from%20one%20of%20those%20caches.%20Then%20re-validate%20and%20re-render.&repo=ai4curation/ai-gene-review)

**4. The most useful `suggested_questions` entry was dropped.**

The base review asked: *"Is the ARE RNA-binding activity of AUH functional in the mitochondrial matrix, or does a cytosolic/precursor pool of AUH mediate mRNA regulation?"* That is the central unresolved problem for this gene — AUH is a matrix protein (`GO:0005759`, two Reactome TAS rows + `PMID:24598254` subfractionation), yet the `GO:0003730` IDA rests on binding cytosolic cytokine/proto-oncogene 3'-UTRs (IL-3, GM-CSF, c-fos, c-myc). The replacement question ("Which RNA contacts of AUH are direct in mitochondria…") is narrower and leaves the compartment paradox unstated, even though the review promotes `mRNA 3'-UTR binding` to a core function. Please restore a question covering the compartment mismatch.

### 🔵 SUGGESTION

**5. Core function 2 has no `locations`.** Core function 1 correctly carries `GO:0005759 mitochondrial matrix`; core function 2 (`GO:0003730`) carries none, which sidesteps #4 rather than recording it. If the matrix is where you think the physiologically relevant RNA binding happens, say so; if it is genuinely unresolved, the `description` should say the compartment is unresolved (it currently says only that "physiological RNA targets … remain incompletely resolved").

**6. `PMID:12434311` and `PMID:12655555` are added as references but cited nowhere, and their `findings` carry no `supporting_text`.** `PMID:12434311` (full text available, HTML-extracted) is the strongest available support for two claims the review makes without anchoring them: the reversibility asserted in core function 1's description ("The reaction is reversible; leucine catabolism uses the hydration direction") and the MGCA1 disease link in `description`. A verbatim quote in `core_functions[0].supported_by` would make both checkable. Same applies to the `Reactome:R-HSA-70785` / `R-HSA-9914271` findings and the `PMID:11738050` / `PMID:24598254` / `PMID:34800366` findings, which all have `statement` but no `supporting_text`.

**7. `GO:0006635 UNDECIDED` could say more without overreaching.** The reason says "The tree and MSA have not been assessed". One asymmetry *is* visible in the cached GOA and worth recording: this row's `WITH/FROM` is `PANTHER:PTN000941828` plus ECHS1-type donors (`UniProtKB:P30084`, `MGI:94871`, `RGD:61892`, `RGD:69330`) — a **different** PAINT node from the `PTN000234999` carrying the hydratase and mitochondrion IBDs, and one where AUH is *not* among the donors, unlike `PTN000234999`. Noting that narrows the open question to a specific checkable node placement rather than leaving it as "not assessed".

**8. `PMID:34800366` `relevance` was raised `LOW` → `MEDIUM` with `correctness` kept `VERIFIED`** while `review_notes` state the AUH-specific supplementary row "was not read, so no independent verification of that entry is claimed". The 91 GO:0005515 rows were rewritten, not reactioned. Counts are unchanged: 168 rows, 112 GO:0005515, 91 KEEP_AS_NON_CORE with shared boilerplate. Network is blocked in this runner and the local caches carry labels only, so I confirmed the term exists and is non-obsolete but not the synonym. The notes document the AmiGO/FlyBase lookups and the claim is internally plausible; one QuickGO /complete call would settle it.

Also unchanged: 91 summaries remain accession-only rather than resolving partner gene symbols (moot if they become REMOVE).

Requesting changes on two items; two of the three previous IMPORTANT items are fully resolved and the scientific core is sound.

**Resolved since last round:** additional_reference_ids is now claim-specific (PMID:31951201 on every row whose reason invokes the structure, Reactome cargo events on the GO:0097500 row, no row re-citing its own original_reference_id); the basal-body ACCEPT now links the HPA antibody record with an explicit read boundary; core_functions[0] no longer denies the receptor-localization participation it asserts in directly_involved_in; and ten KEEP_AS_NON_CORE reasons now give positive support instead of guarding against inferences nobody proposed.

I also tried to break the 'connects BBS4 and BBS8' claim and could not. The sentence about the BBS18 helix loosely contacting BBS1's GAE domain is about one protruding subsegment; the paper's structural claim for the protein is 'BBS18 winds through two super-helically arranged TPR domains of the perpendicularly arranged BBS4 and BBS8 subunits, and clamps them together like a U-bolt.' GO:0140378 on that is a good term fit, and all four supporting_text quotes verify verbatim.

**1. IMPORTANT - the MODIFY is applied to a row that merges two different GOA tuples.** BBIP1-ai-review.yaml:118-140. BBIP1-goa.tsv has four GO:0005515 rows, two of them PMID:19081074 - line 8 with UniProtKB:Q96RK4 (BBS4, IntAct) and line 21 with UniProtKB:Q9UBN7 (HDAC6, UniProt). The review carries one entry for both (23 GOA data rows vs 22 source annotations). Under KEEP_AS_NON_CORE that merge was lossy but harmless. MODIFY changes it: the single proposed_replacement_terms value re-terms both GOA rows, including the BBS4 one. The reason text disclaims exactly that ('The BBS4 association ... is not reclassified as deacetylase binding'), but prose cannot carve an exception out of a single-valued slot, there is no with_from slot in the schema to disambiguate, and goa_validator keys on (term, evidence, reference) so it cannot see the dropped row. Split into two GO:0005515/IPI/PMID:19081074 entries - MODIFY to GO:0042826 for HDAC6, REMOVE for BBS4 - which also brings the source count to 23 and matches GOA 1:1. GO:0042826 itself is the right call and the cached abstract supports it verbatim.

**2. IMPORTANT - the two BBS4-only GO:0005515 rows are still KEEP_AS_NON_CORE.** Lines 141-155 and 156-169. protein_binding_policy.py:41 sets COMPLIANT_ACTIONS = {MODIFY, REMOVE, UNDECIDED, PENDING}, and the legacy carve-out is scoped to untouched reviews - the policy says 'apply this policy to new reviews and to annotations touched during re-review', and both rows were rewritten in this commit. The new reasons do not engage it: 'under the supplied ActionEnum' answers which actions the schema permits, not which the policy permits, and 'a supported interaction is not removed solely because its GO term is generic' is conceded by the policy itself ('removal does not mean the reported interaction is false'). No informative MODIFY exists here, so REMOVE is the outcome, with GO:0140378 now carrying the structural content. If the policy is wrong for IPI rows with named partners that is a defensible position, but it should be argued in the policy module and the annotation-reviewer skill rather than worked around per-gene.
